title: Transactional rollout API + client helpers for safe idempotent changes and auto-rollback rules
creator: Aisha Nadeem
description: Add a transactional Rollout API and SDK client helpers that provide idempotent, permission-guarded operations for creating/updating canary and A/B rollouts, plus first-class support for shadowing and configurable auto-rollback triggers. The goal is to make rollout changes atomic, auditable, and recoverable while preventing common operator mistakes (double-apply, conflicting concurrent edits, or insufficient permissions).
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes /v1/rollouts: POST for create, PATCH for update, GET for status with revision metadata and idempotency-key support
All write endpoints accept an Idempotency-Key header and store idempotency results for 24h; duplicate requests return previous response and do not create duplicate rollouts
Patch operations use optimistic concurrency via rollout.revision integer; conflict returns 409 with current revision

SDK provides helpers: RolloutClient.createOrUpdateAtomic(rolloutSpec, idempotencyKey) and a safeApply utility that retries transient conflicts with exponential backoff and surfaces deterministic merge failures
Permission model: 'rollouts.write' for creating/updating; 'rollouts.rollback' for triggering manual rollbacks; console actions and SDK calls are authorized using scoped tokens and audited
Auto-rollback rules are supported in rolloutSpec: metric, threshold, window, minTrafficToEvaluate; auto-rollback executes a transactional rollback and emits an audit event
End-to-end tests for canary traffic split, shadow traffic mirroring, and an auto-rollback triggered by simulated metric regression are green in CI
Documentation page and SDK examples (Python/TS) published, with migration notes for projects using previous rollout APIs
tasks: API: Define request/response payloads, idempotency semantics, error codes (400/401/403/409/422/500), and retention for idempotency records
Server: Implement optimistic concurrency (revision int) and idempotency store in metadata service
Server: Auto-rollback executor that uses same transactional path as manual rollback
SDK: Add RolloutClient.createOrUpdateAtomic helper + safeApply strategy in Python and TypeScript
Permissions: Add 'rollouts.write' and 'rollouts.rollback' scopes; update authz middleware and audit logs
Console: Add rollout creation form fields for auto-rollback policies and show current revision + pending changes
E2E: Add CI scenario that wires a canary, injects synthetic latency/4xxs and asserts auto-rollback
Docs: Migration guide, examples, and troubleshooting section for common conflict errors
QA: Manual runbook test for recovery after stale revision conflict and for idempotency replay behavior
comments: 2025-02-11 - Marcus Chen: Scoped the work to core API + SDK helpers this cycle. Will follow-up with console UX next cycle. Prioritize idempotency + auditability.
2025-02-12 - Priya Khatri (security): We need explicit audit fields written for every state transition (actor, token_id, idempotency_key). Will add to authZ ticket.

2025-02-14 - Aisha Nadeem: Prototype implemented optimistic concurrency. Observed race when two clients attempt to promote canary -> prod simultaneously; designed safeApply retry up to 3 times then fail with merge guidance.

2025-02-16 - Jordi Alvarez (SRE): Auto-rollback executor should prefer 'graceful fallback' (reduce traffic to baseline) before full rollback to limit churn. Added task to implement staged rollback option.

2025-02-18 - Marcus Chen: Reviewed SDK helper API; suggested we return a structured result with 'applied': true|false, 'action': 'created'|'updated'|'noop' and 'revision' to make client idempotency handling simpler.

2025-02-19 - Aisha Nadeem: Integration tests added. Simulated metric regression triggers auto-rollback; audit event emitted to /v1/audit and email alert hits on-call. Observability metrics: rollout.rollback.count and rollout.rollback.reason emitted.
notes: Design choices: 1) Use 24h idempotency record TTL to balance storage vs. safety for common client retries. 2) Expose both a simple SDK helper for common flows and a lower-level client for advanced use (partial updates, staged rollout scripts). 3) Auto-rollback policies are evaluated by the metrics-processor service; playbooks will be created for noisy signals. Migration: projects using the legacy rollout API should switch to createOrUpdateAtomic to avoid duplication when re-sending requests from CI.
examples: TS SDK snippet: await client.safeApply(rolloutSpec, { idempotencyKey: 'deploy-20250220', retries: 3 })
Auto-rollback policy example: { metric: 'error_rate_p95', threshold: 0.05, window_sec: 300, min_traffic: 0.02, action: 'rollback' }
